title: Zul'Farrak
body: Zul'Farrak is the city of the Sandfury trolls, and inside its walls the desert sky still stands open overhead. Streets of sand wind between temples of old stone, past graves and shrines and a great stepped pyramid, and the Sandfury hold all of it. Their blood drinkers and shadowcasters, witch doctors, shadowhunters and soul eaters fall on any outsider they find. They do not hold the city alone. Scarabs swarm over the sands, and basilisks crawl among the ruins, their stares stiffening flesh like stone. The tribe's rulers keep to places of their own within, and its holy places are closely guarded. Still the outsiders come. Goblins and gnomes want things that can be had only here, a scholar wants writings carried into the city long ago, a mage wants back what the trolls stole from her, and some come for nothing more than the treasure trolls are said to hoard.

title: The Sacred Pool
body: Deep in Zul'Farrak lies a broad sheet of still water, the sacred pool of the Sandfury, a strange sight in a city of sand. Trolls of the tribe keep watch along its banks, blood drinkers, witch doctors and shadowhunters among them, and a hydromancer of the tribe walks the shore as if the water were hers to command. At the edge of the pool hangs a great gong. What it is for, the trolls do not tell outsiders.

title: Theka the Martyr
body: Theka the Martyr died long ago, yet he still walks Zul'Farrak. An undead troll, he paces the ground about his tomb, and the city's scarabs gather there in their dozens. It is said they were once his persecutors, cursed into the shape of the beetles that now scuttle about his shrine. A carved tablet stands beside his resting place. What made him a martyr, and to whom, the city does not tell outsiders.

parts.body: Theka fought as a dead thing fights, laying a fevered plague on those around him that went on burning in their blood. As his wounds mounted his body changed, swelling larger, and for a time neither blade nor shadow could harm him. The change did not last, and the martyr fell at last beside his tomb.

parts.body: The first tablet of Mosh'aru had lain with Theka. Taken from the martyr, it went to Steamwheedle Port together with its twin, and the troll mystic Yeh'kinya received them gladly. He would fuse the ancient tablets together, he said, and study their hidden secrets, and he told their bearer that his debt to them was growing.

title: Witch Doctor Zum'rah
body: Witch Doctor Zum'rah keeps his sanctum at the edge of a troll graveyard, where shallow graves crowd the sand on every side and a cauldron bubbles over its fire beside his chest. Left alone he stands quietly among the graves and pays no heed to those who pass at a distance. His sanctum, though, is his own, and anyone who sets foot in it answers to him.

parts.body: Zum'rah met those who stepped into his sanctum with fury, demanding how they dared. He loosed volleys of shadow and planted a ward from which skeletons rose one after another to fight for him, and he closed his own wounds with healing waves. Over each foe who fell he called on the sands to consume them. In the end the witch doctor fell among his graves.

title: Hydromancer Velratha
body: Hydromancer Velratha is a mystic of the Sandfury who commands water, a rare gift in a city of sand. She walks the shore of the sacred pool deep in Zul'Farrak, following the water's edge as if it were her own, while warriors and witch doctors of her tribe keep watch along the banks around her. Whoever comes to the pool comes before her, and she does not let strangers walk its shore unchallenged.

parts.body: Velratha fought with the cold of deep water, hurling bolts of frost at her foes and turning healing waves on any troll beside her who faltered. The pool she kept could not save her, and the hydromancer fell on its shore.
sources: smart_scripts 7795 (Frostbolt; Healing Wave on a friend missing health), the same spells in the module's dungeon_zulfarrak.sql

parts.body: The second tablet of Mosh'aru had been in Velratha's keeping. Taken from the hydromancer, it went with its twin to the troll mystic Yeh'kinya in Steamwheedle Port, who meant to fuse the two ancient tablets together and study the secrets hidden in them.

parts.body: The Tiara of the Deep, which Velratha's agents had stolen from the mage Tabetha, went home to Dustwallow. Tabetha was delighted to have it back, and as glad that Velratha no longer had it as she was of the jewel itself. She declared herself forever in her helper's debt, and asked them to pay no mind if she had sounded a little mean before: she is a much nicer person, she says, to those who have not stolen from her.

title: Gahz'rilla
body: Gahz'rilla is a huge beast of Zul'Farrak. He dwells in the sacred pool deep within the troll city, a still water in the middle of the desert, and from that pool he can be called up to face any who would challenge him. The trolls keep the manner of his summoning a close secret, and whoever would stand before Gahz'rilla must first wrest it from them.

parts.body: In the Shimmering Flats the gnome Wizzle Brassbolts wants a scale of Gahz'rilla. The beast is so fierce, he says, that even his scales crackle with energy, and it is that energy he hopes to harness for his racing car, if someone will bring him the electrified scale.
sources: quest 2770 description (his scales crackle with energy; harness it for my car; bring me the electrified scale)
thousand_needles.json 40022 (Wizzle and the rocket car)

parts.body: The great gong at the edge of the pool was struck, and the water answered. Gahz'rilla rose from the depths, a hydra of enormous size, and waded ashore before he turned on those who had called him. He fought with the cold of the deep, hurling icicles that slowed his foes, freezing them solid where they stood and slamming into them with a force that flung them back. At last the hydra fell on the shore of his pool.

title: Antu'sul
body: Antu'sul, the Overseer of Sul, is a troll who keeps the basilisks of Zul'Farrak, and he calls them his children. He waits apart from the city's busy streets with young basilisks about his feet, and the Sul'lithuz that crawl through the ruins are of his brood. He does not wait for visitors to reach him. Anyone who comes near his place finds the overseer and his children already coming to meet them.

parts.body: Antu'sul greeted intruders as a meal: lunch had arrived, he told his beautiful children, and they were to tear it to pieces. Basilisk servants rose at his call to defend their master, and more came as he was wounded. He fought as a shaman, with chain lightning and shocks of earth, totems that held his foes fast and wards that healed him. At the last he cried for the children of Sul to protect him, but the overseer fell all the same.

title: Nekrum Gutchewer
body: Nekrum Gutchewer is a troll of Zul'Farrak who has not let death stop him. Undead, he fights for the Sandfury still, a dead warrior who has not given up his place in his tribe. He keeps no hall of his own and is not met walking the city's streets. He comes only when the tribe gathers its warriors against intruders at the great pyramid, and he stands among the last and strongest of them.

parts.body: Nekrum met his foes with a charge that bowled them over, then laid a fevered plague on those around him and hamstrung any who tried to slip away from him. He fought at the foot of the great pyramid's stairs among the last of the Sandfury host, and there he fell.

title: Chief Ukorz Sandscalp
body: Chief Ukorz Sandscalp rules Zul'Farrak from above it. His seat is a high terrace over the city, reached only past a heavy door not far from the great pyramid, and great serpents and hulking basilisks keep guard there with him. At his side stands Ruuzlu, a Sandfury warrior with axe in hand. No outsider reaches the chief of the Sandfury without first finding a way through that door.

parts.body: Ukorz met intruders as a chief of the desert. He roared that the Sandfury reign supreme and that his foes would feel the fury of the sands, and he fought in a berserker's stance, cleaving through those before him; as his wounds mounted he fell into a frenzy. It was not enough. The chief of Zul'Farrak fell on his own high seat, above the city he ruled.
sources: creature_text 7267 groups 1 and 2 (Feel the fury of the sands!; The Sandfury reign supreme!), both said with and without the module (base: group 2 on aggro, group 1 with Frenzy at 30 percent; module: groups 1 and 2 with Frenzy at 60 and 30 percent, group 0 on aggro)

title: Sergeant Bly
body: Sergeant Bly is a human, the leader of a band of adventurers who came to Zul'Farrak, and the trolls caught them. Bly and his companions, Raven, Oro Eyegouge, Murta Grimgut and the goblin Weegli Blastfuse, were caged atop the great pyramid, and the trolls mean to sacrifice them. From his cage Bly pleads with any who will listen: get them out, and he will give his rescuers anything they want.

parts.body: Bly's gratitude did not last. When the fighting was done he thanked his rescuers, then told them to forget anything he might have said about repaying them. Called out for it, he flared up, demanding how they dared say such a thing to him; after all they had been through, he declared, he had never liked them anyway. Those of his band still standing took his side and turned on their rescuers, but Bly himself fell.

title: The Prisoners of the Pyramid
body: The great pyramid of Zul'Farrak rises in broad steps above the sand, and a long stair climbs its face to the platform at its top. There the Sandfury keep their prisoners, shut in cages, and an executioner of the tribe stands over them. In the cages waits a band of adventurers the trolls have taken, two humans, an orc, a dwarf and a goblin, and every one of them wants out. The trolls do not mean to let their captives go, and whoever would free them must first deal with the guard who stands over the cages.

parts.body: The goblin of the band, Weegli Blastfuse, has a bargain to offer whoever helps them: he can blow up the door that leads to the chief of Zul'Farrak. With that door down, he makes plain, nothing would stand between them and the troll chief himself.
sources: npc_text 1511 (if you get me out of here, I can blow up the door that leads to the chief of Zul'Farrak), 1513 (kill enough and I'll blow the door to the troll chief) and 1514 (the only thing between us and the chief troll is that door), the three menus of gossip 940

parts.body: The executioner met any who came to stop him with a cry that the executions should begin, and over each foe who fell he declared that justice was done. He fell beside the cages all the same, and on his body was the key that opened them.
sources: creature_text 7274 (Let the executions begin!, on aggro; Justice is done!, on kill), base and module
creature_loot_template 7274: Executioner's Key 8444, 100 percent; Troll Cages 141070-141074 lock 420 (key 8444)

parts.body: When the cages opened, the freed band took its stand at the top of the stairs, and Weegli saw what was coming: here they come! Below, the Sandfury massed in the courtyard, slaves and drudges, cretins, acolytes and zealots, and climbed the stairs in ever larger groups. A second host followed the first. When it too was broken, Bly cried that it was time to move forward, and the band went down the stairs to meet the last of them at the foot of the pyramid, led by a shadowpriest and an undead troll.
sources: go_troll_cage (zulfarrak.cpp: on opening, the band walks to the top of the stairs at 1882-1891, 1263-1272, z 41)
npc_weegli_blastfuse (on arrival, creature_text 7607 group 0, Oh no! Here they come!)

parts.body: The shadowpriest Sezz'ziz led the last host, and Bly went straight for him, calling his band after him. Sezz'ziz hurled bolts of shadow, sent his foes reeling in terror with a psychic scream and healed the trolls around him, while fresh zealots and acolytes kept coming at his call. He fell at the foot of the stairs all the same.
sources: zulfarrak.cpp npc_sergeant_bly MovementInform (at the descent point Bly attacks Sezz'ziz and calls for help within 100 yards)
zulfarrak.cpp npc_shadowpriest_sezziz (Shadow Bolt, Psychic Scream, Renew and Heal on the most wounded friend, summons Sandfury Zealots 8877 and Acolytes 8876 every 10-14 s)

title: The Scarabs of Zul'Farrak
body: Scarabs swarm through Zul'Farrak. They scuttle along its streets and among its ruins in ones and twos, and in places they gather in their dozens. Each is small and hard of shell, but they come together, and a cloud of plague rises about them that saps the strength, quickness and wits of anyone caught in it. The trolls of the city do not trouble them, nor do the scarabs trouble the trolls, and the beetles go about their business among the graves and ruins as if the city were as much theirs as the tribe's.

parts.body: In Gadgetzan the goblin Tran'rek prizes those shells. They are hard enough to build with, so useful that the scarabs of Tanaris were hunted nearly to extinction, and he knew a colony still thrived in Zul'Farrak, where the trolls do not hunt them for their shells. The uncracked shells reached him in good time, for his cousin in Booty Bay was growing impatient, and he called their bringer a real lifesaver.
sources: quest 2865 description (very hard shells; building material; hunted to near extinction; a colony in Zul'Farrak; the trolls don't hunt them for their shells), completion text (my cousin in Booty Bay, getting impatient) and reward text (a real lifesaver)

title: The Sandfury
body: Zul'Farrak is the Sandfury's city, and its streets belong to the tribe's warriors and mystics. Blood drinkers leech the life from their foes, and shadowcasters wrap themselves in demon skin and hurl bolts of shadow. Witch doctors plant totems that spout lava and wards that heal the trolls around them, and they mend their wounded kin with quick prayers. Shadowhunters shoot down those at a distance and hex their foes, and soul eaters bite at the souls of their enemies while dark offerings heal their kin. Badly hurt, many of them break off and run, only to come back with others at their side.

parts.body: In Gadgetzan, the smith Trenton Lighthammer prizes one of the tribe's crafts. The Sandfury make a tempering agent from sandstones, and connoisseurs value the goods tempered with it, so he asked for a good supply. When twenty vials of troll temper were set before him, he was delighted: he would be at work for days, he said, before he had used it all.
sources: quest 3042 description (tempering agent from sandstones; highly prized by connoisseurs) and reward text (at work for days)

parts.body: Sandarr Dunereaver is seldom found in the city, but when he walks its streets he is a warrior to be feared. He met his foes with a shout that sapped their strength, struck hard and pummeled any who tried to cast a spell, and when he appeared he fell like the rest.
sources: creature 10080 single spawn on map 209 at 1546,1015; smart_scripts 10080 (despawns at spawn 90 percent of the time; Demoralizing Shout, Strike, Pummel), not changed by the module

parts.body: Dustwraith is a Sandfury seldom seen. Where he appeared he fought like an assassin, striking with sinister blows and leaving a virulent poison in his victims' blood, until he was cut down.

parts.body: Zerillis is rarely seen among the Sandfury, a hunter who keeps his distance. Where he appeared he shot at his foes from afar, slowed them with shots of frost and caught them in his net, and he was brought down at last.
